sources.entry: 9. Performance Analysis and Tuning on Modern CPUs - Walks from a noisy timing to counters to a named bottleneck, applying roofline and top-down to whole programs.

summary.one_liner: The source repository for the book "Performance Analysis and Tuning on Modern CPUs" by Denis Bakhvalov, which is built into a PDF from Markdown with pandoc and LaTeX.
summary.what_it_does: The README covers only the build process, not the book's content. It explains how to generate book.pdf by running export_book.py, then pdflatex, bibtex, and pdflatex again. It lists the required tools: Python 3 with the natsort module, pandoc 2.9, pandoc-fignos, pandoc-tablenos, pandoc-crossref, and MiKTeX. It also gives separate commands for Linux/Windows cmd and Windows PowerShell. The README does not describe the book's chapters or topics beyond the title, so the listing's description (roofline, top-down, counters) is not confirmed by this file.
use_cases: build the perf book PDF from source
compile Markdown book with pandoc and LaTeX
learn CPU performance analysis from a free book
read a book on roofline and top-down analysis
how_to_run: Install pandoc 2.9 and pandoc-crossref manually, and MiKTeX
python export_book.py && pdflatex book.tex && bibtex book && pdflatex book.tex && pdflatex book.tex
On Windows PowerShell, wrap the same commands in a block that sets $ErrorActionPreference="Stop"
notable: Book is written in Markdown and compiled to PDF through pandoc and LaTeX
Explicit build steps for both Linux/Windows cmd and Windows PowerShell
Content is released under Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal
caveats: PDF build works on Windows and Linux; macOS needs pandoc-crossref and other components built from source
The first PDF compilation may be slow
